text: @sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 MySQL 凭据存储插件，接入 credentials 服务并将 refs 与 records 两类凭据数据持久化到数据库。它实现凭据解析、描述、写入、删除、记录枚举和原子修改，并在启动时创建和校验所需表结构。可选配置字段加密密钥后，凭据字段以 AES-256-GCM 加密存储。适合需要在 MySQL 中集中保存 DSH 凭据的部署；需要配置 MySQL 主机、用户、密码、数据库和表前缀。

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql stores DSH credential refs and records in MySQL. The credentials provider can resolve, read, write, list, and modify them, and initializes its tables at startup. An optional key enables AES-256-GCM field encryption. MySQL settings are required.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql 的功能「凭据引用存储」：通过 credentials 服务读写、描述和删除引用值，并持久化到 MySQL。
@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql 的功能「凭据记录管理」：读取、描述、列举和删除 API key 或 grant 记录；枚举结果包含记录键和类型，不返回记录值。
@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql 的功能「事务式记录修改」：调用 modifyRecord 时在数据库事务内锁定目标记录、交给回调修改，再提交更新后的记录。
@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql 的功能「凭据字段加密」：配置加密密钥后，字段加密器使用 AES-256-GCM 生成带版本标记的密文，并在读取时解密。
@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql 的功能「数据库表初始化」：插件初始化时创建 refs、records 与版本表，并检查已应用 schema 版本；可配置是否自动迁移。

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · @sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql：

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · @sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql：The **MySQL credentials vault** for the DeepSeek Harness — a concrete `CredentialProvider` (the `dsh-credentials` seam). Load it as a plugin; it registers `ctx.credentials` and persists both key spaces (refs and records) into MySQL, behavior-contract-equivalent to `dsh-credentials-local`, with **optional field-level AES-256-GCM encryption**.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Companion plugins (distributed dsh deployment)：This MySQL vault is the credentials component of a **shared-MySQL distributed dsh
deployment**, designed to run alongside three sibling plugins — `dsh-workspace-bootstrap`,
`dsh-storage-mysql`, and `dsh-session-persistence-mysql` — which switch the default
workspace / storage / session-persistence backends to shared MySQL (this plugin switches
the credentials backend):

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Companion plugins (distributed dsh deployment)：| Plugin | GitHub repository | npm package page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@sandersyao/dsh-workspace-bootstrap` | https://github.com/sandersyao/dsh-workspace-bootstrap | https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sandersyao/dsh-workspace-bootstrap |
| `@sandersyao/dsh-storage-mysql` | https://github.com/sandersyao/dsh-storage-mysql | https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sandersyao/dsh-storage-mysql |
| `@sandersyao/dsh-session-persistence-mysql` | https://github.com/sandersyao/dsh-session-persistence-mysql | https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sandersyao/dsh-session-persistence-mysql |

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Guides：- **Try it in a dsh profile without touching existing credentials** — `docs/DSH_PROFILE_TRIAL.md`.
- **Production / npm install & `cordis.patch.yml` integration (replace the default file provider)** — `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` §8.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Configuration：Credentials, table prefix and the encryption key come from environment variables / a `.env` file (see `.env.example`). **Independent `CREDENTIALS_*` win; they fall back to the shared `MYSQL_*`** — reuse the same connection when co-existing with `dsh-session-persistence-mysql`, or configure independently. The plugin `Config` is fully optional — environment is the source of truth for credentials (never hard-code a password).

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Configuration：| Env | Fallback | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CREDENTIALS_HOST` | `MYSQL_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | MySQL host. |
| `CREDENTIALS_PORT` | `MYSQL_PORT` | `3306` | Port. |
| `CREDENTIALS_USER` | `MYSQL_USER` | — (required) | Least-privilege DB user. |
| `CREDENTIALS_PASSWORD` | `MYSQL_PASSWORD` | — (required) | Password. |
| `CREDENTIALS_DATABASE` | `MYSQL_DATABASE` | — (required) | Target database. |
| `CREDENTIALS_TABLE_PREFIX` | `MYSQL_TABLE_PREFIX` | — (required) | Table prefix; validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; base names distinct from session tables to avoid collision. |
| `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | `ENCRYPTION_KEY` | (empty) | Field-encryption key; empty = plaintext (startup warning). |
| `CREDENTIALS_SSL_REQUIRED` | `MYSQL_SSL_REQUIRED` | `false` | Reserved for TLS enforcement (deferred). |
| `CREDENTIALS_POOL_SIZE` | `MYSQL_POOL_SIZE` | `10` | Pool sizing. |
| `CREDENTIALS_SCHEMA_AUTO_MIGRATE` | `MYSQL_SCHEMA_AUTO_MIGRATE` | `true` | Auto-migrate schema on startup; `false` only validates. |

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Configuration：> **Test isolation.** Automated tests (`vitest`) run against a **separate** database to avoid touching the production one: `CREDENTIALS_TEST_DATABASE` (default `test`) overrides `CREDENTIALS_DATABASE` during tests, and `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` is used only by the test harness to create/grant the test DB. See `docs/MANUAL_TEST_PLAN.md`.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Storage layout：Three tables, all under `CREDENTIALS_TABLE_PREFIX`:

- `${prefix}credential_refs` — the refs space: `ref_name`(PK) + `value`.
- `${prefix}credential_records` — the records space: `rec_key`(`<scope>/<id>`, PK) + `kind` + `payload`(JSON).
- `${prefix}credential_meta` — applied schema version.

The base names deliberately differ from `dsh-session-persistence-mysql`'s `sessions` / `events` / `_meta`, so **even sharing a database and prefix causes no collision**.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Resolution layering (contract-equivalent to dsh-credentials-local)：```text
inherited process environment   (read-only, always wins)
> MySQL managed store           (writable)
> project .env → user .env
```

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Schema & migration：Startup performs a connection test + idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, then reads `${prefix}credential_meta`; an applied version higher than expected fails closed (downgrade unsupported). With `CREDENTIALS_SCHEMA_AUTO_MIGRATE=false`, a version mismatch fails instead of migrating.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Field encryption (vault feature)：When `CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set (32-byte hex or any string, key derived via SHA-256):
- ref values and a record's `key` / `env` / `payload` are **AES-256-GCM** encrypted before write (per-row random IV + auth tag); the key is **never stored in the DB and never logged**.
- Storage uses a versioned envelope string (`v1:<iv>.<cipher+tag>`); plaintext data is unaffected.
- Without a key it's plaintext mode (startup warning); the switch does not change the seam's behavior contract (values still round-trip).

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Model experience：Indirect, through the LLM adapters that consume it: a resolved value authorizes an adapter's request to its provider; all model-visible surfaces are the adapter's responsibility. Credentials never enter the request prefix.

@sandersyao/dsh-credentials-mysql README · Known limitations & deferred items：- **No hot-publishing of external edits** — no file watcher; rows changed directly in MySQL are picked up by consumers' per-operation re-resolution (the seam already resolves per operation, so this is usually invisible).
- **`set`/`unset` reject while shadowed by the environment** (seam rule, same as the local provider).
- **No automatic migration from `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`** — switching providers does not import the old file into MySQL (see `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` §8.3).
- **TLS / transport deferred** — `CREDENTIALS_SSL_REQUIRED` is a reserved bit.
- **Peer ranges target the dsh `v0.1.5-rc.1` line** (`^0.1.5-rc.1`); re-align `peerDependencies` when the official seam release moves on.
